initial.title: [C-SDLC v2] Make doctor honor split issue and code repository authority
initial.goal: Make csdlc-doctor validate issue-tracker and code-publication repository authority separately without weakening drift detection.
initial.required_outcome: Doctor accepts same-repository topology and the explicit supported split-authority topology, rejects accidental repository drift, and active operator guidance describes the contract accurately.
declared_scope: Typed C-SDLC v2 repository identity model used by doctor
Doctor readiness and repository drift diagnostics
Focused same-repository, valid split-repository, and invalid-drift tests
Active C-SDLC v2 skills and runbooks that describe repository identity
authority_boundary: Issue #45 changes only C-SDLC v2 doctor identity validation and directly coupled typed contracts
The source issue repository and code/PR repository remain independently authoritative
Remote names are evidence labels, not authority
No repository migration or legacy issue mutation is part of this issue
operator_constraints: Never write tracked issue work on main
Use only typed C-SDLC v2 Rust lifecycle tools
Do not infer split authority from an incidental remote mismatch
Update all active skills and runbooks affected by the contract
Treat time, token, and line-count estimates as reviewable rather than hard limits
initial.task_boundary: Represent or derive issue and code repository authority separately for doctor, prove the three required identity cases, and update directly affected active guidance.
deliverables: Typed split-authority identity contract available to doctor
Fail-closed doctor decision logic with specific drift diagnostics
Updated active skills and operator runbooks
Exact-head review and focused validation evidence
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Doctor accepts a same-repository lifecycle record whose issue repository and effective code remote normalize to the same identity
AC-2: Doctor accepts the supported split route only when issue repository danielbaustin/agent-design-language and code repository agent-logic/agent-design-language are both explicit and consistent
AC-3: Doctor rejects absent, partial, substituted, or mismatched split-authority identity with repository_identity_drift and a specific diagnostic
AC-4: Focused deterministic tests cover same-repository acceptance, valid split-repository acceptance, and invalid drift rejection
AC-5: Active C-SDLC v2 skills and runbooks consistently explain separate issue and code repository authority without reviving claims or sunset v1 routes
AC-6: Typed card, schema, focused Rust, and strict lint validation pass within recorded reviewable budgets
dependencies: Merged split-authority publication support from issue #3
Preserved legacy tracker issue #5895 as observed defect evidence
non_goals: Changing GitHub publication or merge semantics beyond the identity input doctor consumes
initial.plan_summary: Model the two repository authorities explicitly, teach doctor a three-way fail-closed decision, add focused fixtures for all required cases, update active guidance, validate, and obtain exact-head review.

steps.action: Trace the current doctor, record, publication, and Git-remote identity flow and select the smallest typed split-authority representation.
Implement same-repository and explicit split-repository validation with specific fail-closed drift diagnostics.
Add deterministic fixtures and tests for same repository, valid split authority, and invalid drift.
Update every active skill and runbook affected by repository identity, then run focused validation and exact-head review.

invariants: Issue and code repository identities never collapse implicitly
Explicit consistent split authority is required when identities differ
Effective Git topology cannot substitute for issue authority
Same-repository compatibility remains deterministic and fail-closed
No claims, leases, v1 wrappers, or migration assumptions return
risks: A permissive fallback accidentally accepts arbitrary origin drift
Identity normalization treats distinct repositories as equal
The record schema duplicates publication identity inconsistently
Skills or runbooks continue teaching the obsolete single-repository assumption
stop_conditions: The implementation requires guessing either repository identity
A split route cannot be represented without ambiguity
Scope expands into repository migration or unrelated lifecycle repair

validation_lanes.proof_role: Focused Rust fixtures prove same-repository acceptance, explicit valid split acceptance, and accidental drift rejection.
Typed validation, active guidance scans, and strict Clippy prove schema and operator-contract consistency.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on missing or ambiguous repository identity, unexpected effective remote drift, stale typed state, failed three-case proof, or obsolete active guidance.
review_prompts: Can any incidental or attacker-controlled remote mismatch be accepted as a split route?
Are issue and code repository identities sourced from independent explicit authority rather than guessed from origin?
Do the three focused tests distinguish same-repo success, valid split success, and invalid drift failure?
Do all active skills and runbooks teach the new contract consistently without reviving sunset concepts?
Are the time and token estimates sufficient but non-binding?
initial.review_scope: Issue #45 typed repository identity, doctor validation and diagnostics, focused three-case tests, and directly affected active skills/runbooks.
